title: Realization of a Quantum Topological Photon Pump
authors: Qianao Yue, Bernardo Barrera, Martin Ritter, David M. Long, David A. Lane, Anushya Chandran, Alicia J. Kollár
abstract: Topological pumps transfer charge or energy at quantized rates determined solely by band topology, independent of the details of the control fields. Photon pumps operating on this principle could enable the robust preparation of non-classical states in a quantum cavity, even in the presence of control imperfections, but have not been directly observed. We present the first experimental observation of a topological photon pump, using a transmon qubit coupled to a microwave cavity. The pump operates in the quantum regime, pumping up from the vacuum state up to $\approx 7$ photons, and produces demonstrably non-classical cavity states for the first few cycles.
summary: The research reports the first experimental realization of a topological photon pump using a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a microwave cavity. By controlling external fields to induce spectral flow, the system pumps photons into the cavity at a rate quantized by fundamental band topology. This achievement allows for the robust preparation of non-classical quantum states, which is crucial for quantum computing and communication protocols.
main_problem: The primary goal was the experimental observation of a topological photon pump, which transfers photons into a quantum cavity at a rate quantized by band topology.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated this process using a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a microwave cavity, observing quantized pumping rates and generating demonstrably non-classical (sub-Poissonian) cavity states.
method: The experiment utilized circuit QED spectroscopy, measuring the AC Stark shift on the qubit as a function of the photon number in the cavity to infer the pump rate and final state population.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting transmon qubit coupled to a microwave cavity. The dynamics are governed by an effective Hamiltonian derived from the Jaynes-Cummings model, where pumping relies on spectral flow induced by time-varying external fields (detuning $\Delta$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}(t)$).
key_observables: Quantized photon pump rate ($P/P_q \approx 1$), maximum observable photon number ($\langle n angle \approx 7$), and sub-Poissonian photon statistics.
important_parameters: The process requires operating in specific parameter regimes defined by inequalities (e.g., $\kappa \ll \omega < g \ll \Delta, B$) to ensure adiabatic evolution.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the validity of the adiabatic approximation and the ability to maintain a hierarchy of energy scales throughout the pumping cycle.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral flow mechanism (pumping vs. depumping), phase diagrams showing $n_{	ext{max}}$ dependence on control parameters, and spectroscopy plots confirming photon number resolution via AC Stark shifts.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework based on spectral flow, presents the experimental setup using circuit QED, describes the measurement protocol involving adiabatic evolution and subsequent qubit spectroscopy to resolve $n$, and finally reports quantitative measurements of quantized pumping rates and state preparation fidelity.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines topological concepts from condensed matter theory with cutting-edge quantum optics experiments in cavity QED. Demonstrating a robust, topologically protected process for generating non-classical light sources is a major advance for quantum information applications.

figures.caption: Figure 1. The Topological Photon Pump. (a) A coupled qubit- cavity system is periodically driven by a slow external drive with period T. One photon enters the cavity per cycle, so that the average pump rate Pq = 1/T. (b) The instantaneous spectrum vs time, showing spectral flow. Along each colored line, an n-photon state |n, g⟩is adiabatically transported one rung up the eigenstate ladder to an (n + 1)-photon state |n + 1, g⟩in one period; over multiple periods, the number of photons increases from n = 0 to n = nmax. The black lines correspond to depumping states.

Figure 2. Phase Diagram of the Topological Pump. (a) Schematic of the effective time-dependent field ⃗B(t) (blue) relative to the ring | ⃗B(t)| = ∆. (b) The analytically computed maximum photon number nmax (color) as a function of B and ∆for g = 13 MHz, neglecting cavity loss. The resonances at ∆ℓ, where nmax = 0 separate large regions of robust pumping, with the largest values of nmax ≈20 found in the range ∆2 < ∆< ∆1 (blue diamond). Panels (c-f) show data along the black line B = 120 MHz. (c) Experimentally achieved largest photon number nfinal over 11 cycles (circles) and numerically simulated values accounting for cavity decay (red dashed line) versus detuning at B = 120 MHz (black line...

Figure 3. Quantization of Pump Rate. Photon pump rate P/Pq extracted from the first five cycles versus B for ∆= 101, 90, 80 MHz and ω = 5 MHz. Error bars indicate the uncertainty of the fit to n(mT) = (P/κ) × (1 −e−κmT ). We observe P ≈0 for B < Bmin(∆) (gray shaded region) in the trivial regime, and P/Pq ≈1 deep in the topological regime B > Bmin(∆) + 10 MHz. Insets show the drive protocols in the two regimes. Sample spectroscopy data corresponding to ∆= 80 MHz are shown in Fig. S9 of the Supplemental Materials.

Figure 4. Fock-State Pumping. (a-d) Photon-number-resolved qubit spectroscopy after m = 0-3 pump cycles, showing exper- imental data (white circles), coherent-state distributions with |α|2 = m (red), and ideal m-photon Fock states (blue). The upper (lower) axis indicates integer multiples of the single- photon shift χ1 (the exact qubit frequency shifts corresponding to m photons). Despite cavity decay, the measured photon- number distributions retain strong overlap with the 1, 2, and 3-photon Fock states.
